headline: Conversation Rounds Activity - Rotating ESL Role-Play Practice
outcomes: Students practise spontaneous speaking in short, focused rounds instead of one long unfocused chat
Every student gets a turn because the activity rotates roles and keeps the class moving
Listening remains active while classmates perform, because observers can notice useful phrases or strong choices
Teachers can turn almost any topic into repeated role-play practice without writing scenarios manually
howItWorks: LessonCaptain generates a role-play situation connected to the lesson topic
Two students take the active roles while the rest of the class observes with a clear listening focus
After a short round, the teacher rotates roles or changes the scenario constraint
The class reflects on useful language, then runs another round with stronger phrasing
teacherUseCases: Business English practice such as client calls, job interviews, complaints, or negotiations
Conversation classes where students need structure but not a full scripted dialogue
Small-group speaking lessons where everyone needs repeated chances to perform

faq.q: How is Conversation Rounds different from Scenario Simulator?
faq.a: Conversation Rounds is lighter and more repeatable. It focuses on short role-play turns and rotation, while Scenario Simulator builds a longer branching situation with roles and consequences.

faq.q: Can I use this with one student?
faq.a: It is designed for at least two students so learners can perform with each other. In a one-on-one lesson, the teacher can take the second role, but the group rotation is lost.

faq.q: Do observers have anything to do?
faq.a: Yes. The teacher can give observers a listening focus such as useful phrases, politeness, problem-solving moves, or one improvement for the next round.

faq.q: Which lesson topics fit Conversation Rounds?
faq.a: Any topic with a social or practical situation works: travel problems, workplace decisions, school issues, customer service, interviews, planning, or disagreements.

faq.q: How do students join a Conversation Rounds lesson?
faq.a: No. Students join through the lesson link and participate from any browser without student accounts.
